# Interactions {#sec-interactions}

::: {.callout-note}
This chapter is planned: it states the question and the method. Results will replace the plan as the
analysis is done.
:::

Up to here every account acted alone. The next rung asks who works with whom, and who against whom, using
only where and when people placed.

## The question

Two accounts that keep placing the same colour on the same pixels are probably working together; two that keep
undoing each other are probably not. Can the log alone recover a network of collaboration and conflict?

## Why it matters

The canvas is a shared environment that people both read and write: what you see is what others did. Coordination
through a shared environment is called **stigmergy** (*established*; Grassé 1959 for termite nests, generalised by
Heylighen 2016, see @sec-reading). A network built from co-placement is the most direct way to see who coordinates
with whom without anyone talking.

## Plan

- A bipartite network of accounts and pixels (an edge when an account places the pixel's current colour).
- Its projection onto accounts, with weights that discount very busy pixels.
- **Null:** the configuration model (same degrees, random wiring), so that structure is only read in where it beats
  degree alone.
